source.title: Open Problems on Syzygies and Hilbert Functions

accepted.question_text: For a prime homogeneous ideal P contained in the square of the homogeneous maximal ideal (x1,...,xn)^2 of the standard graded polynomial ring S = k[x1,...,xn], is Castelnuovo-Mumford regularity bounded by degree minus codimension plus one, namely reg(P) <= deg(S/P) - codim(S/P) + 1?
For a prime homogeneous ideal P contained in (x1,...,xn)^2 in S = k[x1,...,xn], is the largest degree of an element in a minimal homogeneous generating set of P at most deg(S/P)?

Find classes of prime homogeneous ideals P contained in (x1,...,xn)^2 for which equality holds in the Eisenbud-Goto regularity bound, so that reg(P) = deg(S/P) - codim(S/P) + 1 for every ideal P in the class.

Construct families of homogeneous ideals whose regularity grows polynomially, exponentially, or doubly exponentially in the number of variables while the largest degree among the minimal homogeneous generators remains bounded by a fixed constant.

Let I be a homogeneous ideal in S with minimal homogeneous generator degrees a1 >= ... >= ap >= 2, and let r = codim(S/I). Find natural sufficient conditions on I that imply reg(S/I) <= a1 + ... + ar - r, or perhaps a bounded multiple of that expression.
For homogeneous ideals I satisfying specified special hypotheses, find sharp upper bounds for reg(I) in terms of the largest degree of an element in a minimal homogeneous generating set of I.
Given a homogeneous ideal I in S and an arbitrary linear form f, is reg(I + (f)) bounded by a polynomial, possibly quadratic, function of reg(I)?
Find classes of ideals I for which the regularity of the radical is no larger than the regularity of the ideal, reg(rad(I)) <= reg(I).
Is reg(rad(I)) bounded by some function, possibly a polynomial function, of reg(I) for homogeneous ideals I?
For finitely generated graded S-modules M and N, is reg(Tor_i^S(M,N)) bounded in terms of reg(M) and reg(N), perhaps after imposing additional hypotheses on M and N?
Find classes of ideals for which one can obtain useful upper bounds on the regularity of intersections of ideals in those classes.
Find classes of ideals for which one can obtain useful upper bounds on the regularity of products of ideals in those classes.
Find classes of ideals for which one can obtain useful upper bounds on the regularity of powers, including the regularity of squares of ideals.

Fix natural numbers a1,...,ar. Does there exist a number p, depending only on these degrees, such that for every polynomial ring W over k and every homogeneous ideal J with minimal homogeneous generator degrees a1,...,ar, the projective dimension pd(W/J) is at most p, independently of the number of variables of W?

Fix natural numbers a1,...,ar. Does there exist a number q, depending only on these degrees, such that for every polynomial ring W over k and every homogeneous ideal J with minimal homogeneous generator degrees a1,...,ar, the regularity reg(W/J) is at most q, independently of the number of variables of W?
For a chosen class of homogeneous ideals, obtain good upper bounds on the largest degree of an element in a minimal homogeneous Groebner basis.
Study Castelnuovo-Mumford regularity for graded modules over Koszul rings that are not polynomial rings.
Study the properties of multigraded regularity for multigraded rings, ideals, and modules.

If a homogeneous ideal I in S contains a regular sequence of homogeneous elements with degrees a1,...,aj, does there exist a monomial ideal containing x1^a1,...,xj^aj with the same Hilbert function as I?
If a homogeneous ideal I in S contains a regular sequence of n quadratic forms, does there exist a monomial ideal containing x1^2,...,xn^2 with the same Hilbert function as I?

For generic homogeneous forms f1,...,fr of degrees a1,...,ar in S and I = (f1,...,fr), is the Hilbert series of S/I given by the truncated series product_{i=1}^r (1 - t^ai)/(1 - t)^n, where all terms at and after the first nonpositive coefficient are omitted as specified by Froberg?
For generic homogeneous forms f1,...,fr of prescribed degrees a1,...,ar, determine the generic initial ideal, with respect to reverse lexicographic order, of the ideal (f1,...,fr).
Find a useful characterization of the Hilbert functions that occur for artinian Gorenstein graded algebras.

For quotient rings R = S/I where I is a monomial ideal or projective toric ideal, find classes of I for which Macaulay-type behavior holds over R: every Hilbert function over R is attained by a lex ideal in R.

Let R = S/I where I is a monomial ideal or projective toric ideal, and let p be the largest degree of a minimal homogeneous generator of I. Find classes of such ideals I for which every Hilbert function over R of a graded ideal generated in degrees greater than p is attained by a lex ideal.

Let R = S/I, where I is a monomial ideal or projective toric ideal. For a graded ideal J in R and a lex ideal L with the same Hilbert function, determine when J can be connected to L by a sequence of deformations, and describe the Hilbert scheme parametrizing graded ideals in R with that Hilbert function.

Let R = S/I where I is a monomial or toric ideal, let J be a graded ideal in R, and let L be a lex ideal in R with the same Hilbert function. Find conditions on R or J under which the Betti numbers of J over R are bounded above by those of L, or the Betti numbers of J + I over S are bounded above by those of L + I.

If a graded ideal J in S contains a regular sequence of homogeneous elements of degrees a1,...,aj and there is a lex-plus-powers ideal L containing x1^a1,...,xj^aj with the same Hilbert function as J, are all Betti numbers of L at least the corresponding Betti numbers of J?
Does Gotzmann persistence hold over a Clements-Lindstrom ring C = S/(x1^a1,...,xn^an) with a1 <= a2 <= ... <= an <= infinity?
For a fixed Hilbert function, does there exist an ideal with greatest graded Betti numbers among all Gorenstein artinian graded ideals having that Hilbert function?

Let M be a square-free monomial ideal in S, and let P be the square-free monomial ideal in S that is the generic initial ideal of M over the exterior algebra on the same variables. Are the Betti numbers of M over S always bounded above by the corresponding Betti numbers of P?

Let M be a monomial ideal generated by q monomials of degree p, and let W be the ideal generated by the first q square-free monomials of degree p in reverse lexicographic order, using a larger polynomial ring if needed. Find conditions on M that imply b_i^S(S/W) <= b_i^S(S/M) for every i >= 0.
If P is a projective toric ideal, does S/P have the smallest Betti numbers among all ideals with the same multigraded Hilbert function as P?
For every artinian graded finitely generated S-module M, are the total Betti numbers bounded below by the Koszul ranks, b_i^S(M) >= binomial(n,i) for all i >= 0?
Let I be a homogeneous ideal contained in (x1,...,xn)^2, set R = S/I, and let T be an artinian graded finitely generated R-module. Is b_i^R(T) >= b_i^R(k) for every i >= 0?
For every artinian graded finitely generated S-module M, is the sum of all total Betti numbers at least 2^n?

Let P be a prime homogeneous ideal containing no linear form, with quadratic part spanned by quadrics of rank at most 4, and suppose the 2-linear strand of S/P has length p. Find natural sufficient conditions under which P contains the 2 by 2 minors of a v by w matrix A of linear forms with v + w - 3 = p, with no zero entry, and with no entry made zero by row and column operations.
Determine how the length of the linear strand in the minimal graded free resolution of S/I is related to other invariants of S/I.

For a specified class of homogeneous ideals I contained in (x1,...,xn)^2, find geometric or combinatorial criteria for I to satisfy property N_p, meaning b_{i,i+j}^S(S/I) = 0 for all j >= 2 and all i <= p.
Let r,q >= 3, let V be the q-th Veronese ring in r variables, and let N_p be the usual syzygy vanishing property. If p <= 3q - 3, does V satisfy N_p?
Is there an algorithm or criterion that takes a proposed graded Betti diagram and determines whether some graded S-module has exactly those graded Betti numbers?
When the positions of potentially nonzero Betti numbers are restricted, describe the generators of the semigroup of Betti diagrams of graded finitely generated S-modules.
Determine the possible Hilbert functions of sets of double points in projective space P^{n-1}.
Given a Hilbert function for a set of points in P^{n-1}, determine the possible graded Betti numbers of the defining ideals of point sets with that Hilbert function.
Determine the possible Hilbert functions of sets of points with multiplicity greater than one, including fat point schemes, in projective space P^{n-1}.
If X is a generic set of q points in P^{n-1}, is the defining ideal of X generated in degree one more than the least degree d for which the Hilbert function of X equals q?
If the Stanley-Reisner ring of a simplicial complex Delta is Cohen-Macaulay, is the Alexander dual ideal I_{Delta^vee} componentwise linear?
If I is a square-free monomial ideal such that S/I is Gorenstein, does the h-vector of S/I satisfy the numerical conditions from the g-Theorem?

Let I be a quadratic square-free monomial ideal such that S/I is Gorenstein and Krull dimension 2d. Must the h-vector h_0,...,h_{2d} satisfy the Charney-Davis-Stanley inequality (-1)^d sum_{i=0}^{2d} (-1)^i h_i >= 0?
If S/I is a Cohen-Macaulay integral domain, is its h-vector unimodal?

Find classes of homogeneous ideals for which the total Betti-number sequence is log-concave or unimodal, and find classes for which each strand sequence {b_{i,i+j}^S(S/I)}_{i>=1} is log-concave or unimodal.
For every finitely generated graded R-module, are the Betti numbers eventually nondecreasing?
If the Betti numbers of a finitely generated graded R-module are bounded, must they eventually become constant?
Does there exist a finitely generated graded periodic R-module, meaning one isomorphic to one of its syzygy modules, whose Betti numbers are not constant?
For a finitely generated graded R-module M, is the limit superior of the ratios b_{i+1}^R(M)/b_i^R(M) always finite?
Find classes of graded rings over which every finitely generated graded module has a rational Poincare series.
When the Poincare series of a finitely generated graded module is rational, determine what can be said about its denominator and the roots of that denominator.
Classify the possible asymptotic growth types of Betti-number sequences over quotient rings, and determine whether only polynomial and exponential growth can occur.
If a finitely generated graded R-module M has finite complexity cx_R(M), is cx_R(M) at most the codepth of R?
If a finitely generated graded R-module M has finite complexity c = cx_R(M), does there exist a real constant a such that b_i^R(M)/i^{c-1} converges to a as i tends to infinity?
If the curvature curv_R(M) of a finitely generated graded R-module M equals 1, must M have finite complexity?
If the curvature curv_R(M) of a finitely generated graded R-module M is greater than 1, does there exist a real constant a such that b_i^R(M)/(curv_R(M))^i converges to a as i tends to infinity?
Find classes of finitely generated graded modules whose Betti-number sequences have strong polynomial growth, and classes whose Betti-number sequences have strong exponential growth.

Let G be the minimal free resolution of a finitely generated module over a complete intersection. Can the Eisenbud operators on G be chosen so that they commute asymptotically, after ignoring a sufficiently long initial segment of the resolution?
For a graded minimal free resolution G over R, do there exist a number p and bases of the free modules in G such that every entry in every differential matrix d_i has degree less than p?
Find classes of graded rings R for which one can give a sharp bound on the rate of the residue field k over R.
Find classes of graded rings that are Koszul, meaning equivalently that k has a linear minimal free resolution over the ring or that the ring has rate 1.
Find classes of ideals that have quadratic Groebner bases.
Is the toric ring of every smooth projectively normal toric variety Koszul?
Is the toric ideal of every smooth projectively normal toric variety generated by quadrics?
Let I be generated by generic homogeneous forms f1,...,fr of degrees a1,...,ar and set R = S/I. Determine what can be said about the Poincare series of the residue field k over R.
If I is generated by generic forms and R = S/I, is the Poincare series of k over R determined by the Hilbert series of R?

For a fixed quotient ring R = S/I, with I generated by generic forms or satisfying another natural hypothesis, determine what can be said about the Poincare series of generic finitely generated R-modules.

When I is generated by generic quadrics and both the generators U of I and a homogeneous presentation matrix V vary over their parameter variety X, does the locus where coker(V) over R = S/I has constant Betti numbers contain a nonempty Zariski open set, and does the locus where coker(V) has constant Betti numbers and a nonperiodic minimal free resolution contain a nonempty Zariski open set?

For a fixed quotient ring R = S/I generated by generic quadrics, possibly with extra restrictions, study the locus of presentation matrices V whose cokernel over R has Betti numbers equal to 2 and a nonperiodic minimal free resolution; determine whether that locus contains a nonempty Zariski open set and describe the syzygies of such modules.
Develop new constructions and ideas for minimal free resolutions of monomial ideals and toric ideals.
For a p-Borel fixed monomial ideal with p > 0, describe its minimal free resolution and find formulas for its regularity and Betti numbers, with the resolution considered in characteristic zero.
Find formulas, or at least sharp upper bounds, for the regularity of an edge monomial ideal in terms of properties of its defining graph.
Find formulas, or at least sharp upper bounds, for the regularity or rate of an edge toric ideal in terms of properties of its defining graph.
Develop a theory of infinite cellular resolutions for minimal free resolutions of monomial ideals over quotient rings R = S/I, especially when I is monomial or toric.
For a minimal free resolution G of a monomial ideal over R = S/I, where I is monomial or toric, determine how to compute the Betti numbers of G using appropriate simplicial complexes.
Construct the minimal free resolution G when G resolves a lex ideal over a quotient ring such as a Veronese ring or a Segre ring.
Let C = S/(x1^a1,...,xn^an) with a1 <= a2 <= ... <= an <= infinity be a Clements-Lindstrom ring. Construct the minimal free resolution over C of a Borel ideal.
Study problems that connect properties of subspace arrangements in complex affine space with properties of minimal free resolutions.
Relate the cohomology algebra of the complement C^r minus a subspace arrangement A to Tor-algebras arising from the arrangement.

For a central hyperplane arrangement A with Orlik-Solomon algebra A = E/J over the exterior algebra E, find combinatorial descriptions, at least in special cases, for the graded Betti numbers dim_C Tor_i^E(A,C)_j.
Construct the minimal free resolution, at least in special cases, of the Orlik-Solomon algebra A over the exterior algebra E.
Construct a well-structured nonminimal free resolution, at least in special cases, of the Orlik-Solomon algebra A over the exterior algebra E.
For the Orlik-Solomon algebra A of a central hyperplane arrangement, find a combinatorial description of the graded Betti numbers dim_C Tor_i^A(C,C)_j.

Find a nonsupersolvable central hyperplane arrangement for which the lower central series formula product_{j>=1}(1 - t^j)^{phi_j} = Hilb_A(-t) holds; equivalently, find a Koszul Orlik-Solomon algebra without a quadratic Groebner basis.

For a central hyperplane arrangement, consider the broken-circuit quotient E/T of the exterior algebra E. Formulate and solve analogues of Problems 16.3 through 16.6 for E/T instead of the Orlik-Solomon algebra A.

trace.notes: Resolved zbMATH 5673526 to DOI 10.1216/JCA-2009-1-1-159; Project Euclid was challenged, so matching Cornell author PDF was used.
Mapped 31-page PDF; labeled open-problem regions appear in Sections 3-16.
Extracted 91 labeled conjectures, problems, and open-ended problems.
Rewrote all accepted items as standalone questions with local notation expanded where needed.
No near-duplicate merges were applied; each accepted item corresponds to a distinct labeled source item.
Accepted 91 self-contained page-located items; evidence quote fields use short source anchors rather than extended verbatim statements.
